speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry in view of the impending takeover of Kopitiam by NTUC Enterprise (a) how will the Government ensure that cooked food prices remain low and affordable; and (b) whether this takeover violates the anti-competition rules.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the proposed acquisition of the Kopitiam food operator chain by NTUC Enterprise will result in a substantial lessening of competition; and (b) whether the acquisition will be suspended pending the approval of the Competition Commission of Singapore, so as to avoid a repeat of the situation with Grab's acquisition of Uber's Southeast Asian operations where its impact on ride-hailing platform services in Singapore could not be reversed.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: There are many factors influencing food prices, such as cost of raw materials and manpower costs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Instead, we focus our efforts on helping Singaporeans to have access to affordable food options.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Such measures will allow consumers to make informed purchasing decisions across a range of cooked food choices.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First question: I read from the report that Kopitiam management will continue to manage those coffee shops.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: If yes, how to achieve a social mission?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Second question: yesterday, I was at Block 504 Kopitiam.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Is it to build up the volume, preparing for this transaction?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Indeed, the precise inner workings of a private enterprise are not immediately within the purview of MTI.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: However, if the Member wishes to file a separate PQ to the relevant agency or agencies, I am sure my colleagues will be happy to oblige as best as they can.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Perhaps, he would like to check with his colleague in MND or HDB and get back to me.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Indeed, there is a "no wrong door" policy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: As part of the "no wrong door" policy, it is also incumbent on us to advise Members if the question may best be answered by a department with the appropriate knowledge, competency, understanding and jurisdiction.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I seek the Member's understanding on this, please.
